headline: High: shared project-directory workflows and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; no direct isolation is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an audio-speech/docs-only agent with no documented shared channel, but Agent B writes and reads the project directory and uses stdin/stdout. If A’s outputs are copied into B’s prompt or files, B may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Agent A outputs text that is pasted into Agent B prompts or files
IF Agent B parses project files or stdin as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Prefix A output as untrusted data in B prompts
Add a manual review step before B consumes A output
Disable copy-paste of raw A output into B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and reads/writes the project directory; Agent A has no network egress and no data classes touched are listed. A shared workspace is not explicitly shown, but B’s file access plus API calls create a plausible leakage path if A’s content is placed in the same project directory. Because the shared workspace is inferred, not proven, medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF Agent A artifacts are stored in the same project directory as Agent B
IF Agent B uploads file contents or prompts containing those artifacts to a third-party model
mitigations: Store A and B artifacts in separate directories
Avoid placing secrets in the shared project tree
Review B prompts before model calls
Turn off network access for B when handling sensitive files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; Agent A’s writable surfaces are undocumented, but its repo is an agent hub that may emit prompts or files. The pair shares a project-directory concurrency model via B, so overlapping writes are plausible even though A’s write capability is not explicit. Uncertainty about A’s surface escalates this to medium.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B operate on the same project directory
IF both agents write generated artifacts without locking or coordination
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate project directory
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Avoid concurrent runs of A and B
Check for file diffs before each write
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s tool pattern is to write files then offer to run, and it can execute shells with user privileges. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative prompts or code, errors from A can cascade into executed actions or committed files. A’s outputs are not documented as verified, so the pair creates a dangerous default handoff with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A output as the basis for generated code or shell commands
IF B executes or offers to execute code produced from A without independent verification
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Compare A output against source requirements
Run B in a disposable sandbox
Disable auto-execution of generated code
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool use

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles generated source code and OPENAI_API_KEY, while Agent A is docs-only and touches no data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern exists if sensitive code or secrets are placed into B’s project directory. Agent A is not cited for a specific compliance regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are stored in Agent B’s project directory
IF retention or logging policies differ for that data class
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the project directory
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review retention settings for B’s model provider
Use a separate workspace for regulated data
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
